section_summary: This section documents Japanese commemorations during April-May 1934 marking the 80th anniversary of Commodore Matthew C. Perry's 1854 Treaty of Kanagawa, concluding with a December 1939 memorial service program for American civic leader Wallace McKinney Alexander. Despatches and reports from U.S. Ambassador Joseph C. Grew detail extensive celebrations, notably the Black Ship Festival at Shimoda and a major America-Japan Society banquet in Tokyo, highlighting public expressions of Japanese-American goodwill. Enclosures include contemporary press clippings from The Japan Advertiser, speech texts, Grew's candid personal diary excerpt, photographs, and diplomatic correspondence acknowledging messages from Kansai commercial bodies.

subfiles.about: Instruction from Secretary of State Cordell Hull to the American Embassy in Tokyo directing it to thank Kansai organizations for their Perry treaty anniversary greetings.
keywords: Osaka Chamber of Commerce and Industry
subfiles.summary: Hull instructs Tokyo to thank the Japan-America Society of Kansai and the Osaka Chamber for their April 24 goodwill telegram on the 80th anniversary of the Perry treaty.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 58 to the American Embassy in Tokyo Regarding Kansai Good Will Message

subfiles.about: Document file note and excerpt from a periodic political report discussing Japanese announcements of celebrations for the 80th anniversary of the Perry treaty.
subfiles.summary: Report extract on planned Perry treaty 80th anniversary events, a Shimoda festival and Tokyo dinner, seen as showing extraordinary Japanese efforts for friendly ties.
subfiles.title: Document File Note and Report Extract on the 80th Anniversary of the Perry Treaty

subfiles.about: Comprehensive despatch from Ambassador Joseph C. Grew reporting on nationwide 80th anniversary Perry treaty celebrations, with extensive enclosures.
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Joseph C. Grew reports extensively on the genuine and hearty celebrations held throughout Japan marking the 80th anniversary of the first U.S.-Japan treaty and honoring Commodore Matthew C. Perry and Townsend Harris. Grew recounts his journey aboard the Japanese destroyer Shimakaze to the Black Ship Festival at Shimoda, where he participated in Shinto ceremonies, inspected Harris relics at Gyokusen-ji temple, and decorated the graves of five American seamen. The despatch also details an America-Japan Society banquet in Tokyo welcoming Prince Iyesato Tokugawa, and encloses newspaper clippings from The Japan Advertiser with speech transcripts and guest lists, an excerpt from Grew's personal diary, and numerous event photographs.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 772 on the 80th Anniversary Celebrations of the Perry Treaty, with Press Clippings, Diary Excerpts, and Photographs

subfiles.about: Despatch transmitting copies of Ambassador Grew's letters of gratitude to Kansai business and cultural leaders pursuant to Department instructions.
keywords: Osaka Chamber of Commerce and Industry
subfiles.summary: Despatch 759: Grew sends his letters to Ogura and Inabata conveying Hull's thanks for the Perry anniversary goodwill telegram.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 759 Acknowledging Good Will Telegram from Kansai Organizations, with Enclosures

subfiles.about: Document file note and periodic report excerpt summarizing Ambassador Grew's commemorative addresses and Prince Tokugawa's speech.
subfiles.summary: Report extract on Grew's Perry anniversary radio broadcast and luncheon and dinner speeches; Prince Tokugawa says the US, Britain and Japan have distinct Pacific spheres and are not rivals.
subfiles.title: Document File Note and Report Extract on Perry Treaty Celebrations and Speeches

subfiles.about: Despatch transmitting five copies of The Japan Advertiser's commemorative supplement celebrating the 80th anniversary of the Perry treaty.
subfiles.summary: Despatch 797: Grew sends five copies of The Japan Advertiser's May 12, 1934 Perry anniversary supplement.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 797 Transmitting The Japan Advertiser Special Perry Anniversary Supplement

subfiles.about: Memorial service program and biographical tribute honoring American civic and business leader Wallace McKinney Alexander at Tokyo Union Church.
subfiles.from: The America-Japan Society, The Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Japan, The Institute of Pacific Relations, and The Japan-America Relations Committee
subfiles.summary: Memorial service booklet for Wallace Alexander (1869-1939) at Tokyo Union Church, December 13, 1939, with a tribute to his missionary ancestry, business and civic leadership, and Japanese-American friendship work, plus eulogies by Nomura, Ishii, Sakatani, Hatta and Grew.
subfiles.title: Memorial Service Program for Wallace McKinney Alexander
